sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by immunofluorescence/immunoblot in HEK293S and CHO-K1 cells; receptor processing (glycosylation, trafficking) studied with tagged constructs. Functional cAMP signaling assays were performed on the tagged receptor variants in the source study (PMC11880984). SNAP-tagged β1-AR family receptors additionally showed preserved agonist-stimulated functional responses in DMR assays (L9/PMC9246501).
sites.rationale: ADRB1 has no annotated signal peptide; residues 1–55 form the extracellular N-terminal domain and TM1 begins at residue 56, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus. Python confirms residue 1 = M and residue 55 = Q (last EC residue before TM1). All nine ledger lines describe N-terminal tags (MYC, FLAG, HA, SNAP-tag) on full-length membrane-anchored β1-AR without naming a specific residue, so the junction is topology-derived as insert_after_residue=0 (prepend before M1). The 55-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample steric space for a ~15–23 aa ALFA-tag insert, and the convergence of five independent publications across multiple tag types and cell systems gives high confidence. Full-length hβ1AR variants (S49 WT, G49, T29, Q31) carrying an N-terminal MYC tag and a C-terminal FLAG tag were transiently expressed in HEK293S and CHO-K1 cells; surface display of the tagged full-length receptor was confirmed. Corroborated by L1 (same dual-tagged construct in pFT-SMMF), L4/L5 (3xFLAG knock-in mouse Adrb1 with added signal sequence, N-terminal FLAG on mature receptor), L6/L7 (HA tag at amino-terminus of β1-AR in stable COS-1 cells, surface distribution confirmed), L8 (N-terminal FLAG on full-length human β1AR detected by immunoblot), and L9 (SNAP-tag fused to N-terminal domain of β1-AR family GPCRs with surface labeling and DMR functional responses). No ledger line names a specific residue junction; the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this GPCR (no annotated signal peptide; residues 1–55 are extracellular, TM1 begins at residue 56), so the junction is topology-derived as a prepend before M1.

sources.claim: The hβ 1 AR N‐terminal variants [S49 (wild‐type, WT), G49, T29, and Q31] with an N‐terminal MYC and a C‐terminal FLAG tag were expressed transiently in HEK293S (A, B, D, E) or CHO‐K1 (C, D) cells for 24 h.

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines (L1–L9) support the same N-terminal extracellular prepend position on ADRB1. No ledger line names any residue within an extracellular loop (ECL1 121–132, ECL2 197–222, ECL3 350–354) as a tag-insertion site, so no internal sites are proposed. The C-terminal FLAG tag reported in L1/L2/L3 falls within the intracellular C-terminal tail (residues 378–477) and is recorded in other_positions. L9 mentions α1-AR subtypes explicitly in the quote but the clip header states β1-AR family members are included; it is used only as corroboration, not as the primary clip. The HA signal peptide mentioned in L1 is a construct artifact added to drive secretory-pathway insertion; after cleavage it leaves the MYC tag at the extracellular N-terminus, consistent with insert_after_residue=0.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length hβ1AR; residue 477 (V) lies within the intracellular C-terminal tail (topology landmarks: intracellular 378–477), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-display site.
